topic.name: Solving Quadratic Equations With Complex Roots

question.explanation:
First, we write the equation in standard form by bringing all of the terms to the left-hand side. This gives the equation \[ x^2-2x+10=0. \]

We can find the roots of a quadratic equation using the quadratic formula: \[ x = \frac{-b\pm\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a} \]

In this case, the coefficients are $a=1,\, b=-2,$ and $c=10.$ Substituting these values into the quadratic formula, we get \begin{align*} x &= \frac{-(-2)\pm\sqrt{(-2)^2-4(1)(10)}}{2(1)}\\[5pt] &= \frac{2\pm\sqrt{4-40}}{2}\\[5pt] &= \frac{2\pm\sqrt{-36}}{2}\\[5pt] &= \frac{2 \pm 6\,\textrm{i}}{2}\\[5pt] &= 1 \pm 3\,\textrm{i}. \end{align*}

Therefore, the equation has two solutions, $x=1+3\,\textrm{i}$ and $x=1-3\,\textrm{i}.$

example.title: Rearranging and Solving a Quadratic Equation With Complex Roots

question.text: What are the solutions of the equation $(x + 1)^2 = -25?$
question.explanation:
The left-hand side is a perfect square. Therefore, we can solve the equation using the square root method:

\begin{align*} (x+1)^2 &= -25\\[5pt] x+1 &= \pm\sqrt{-25}\\[5pt] x+1 &= \pm 5\,\textrm{i}\\[5pt] x &=-1 \pm 5\,\textrm{i} \end{align*}

Therefore, the equation has two solutions, $x=-1+5\,\textrm{i}$ and $x=-1-5\,\textrm{i}.$

example.title: Solving a Quadratic Equation With Complex Roots by Completing the Square

question.text: What are the solutions of the equation $(x-2)^2 = -36?$
question.explanation:
The left-hand side is a perfect square. Therefore, we can solve the equation using the square root method:

\begin{align*} (x-2)^2 &= -36\\[5pt] x-2 &= \pm\sqrt{-36}\\[5pt] x-2 &= \pm 6\,\textrm{i}\\[5pt] x &=2 \pm 6\,\textrm{i} \end{align*}

Therefore, the equation has two solutions, $x=2+6\,\textrm{i}$ and $x=2-6\,\textrm{i}.$
